channel.title: Bentonville Daily
channel.description: Public records and local institutions, daily.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 26, 2026
item.description:
The Arkansas Community Foundation launched a new program with a $10 million grant to address food insecurity in the state.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider reducing the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would reduce the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from 1% to 0.5%. This is the second reading of Ordinance No. 2017-15.
On the Bella Vista Planning Commission Work Session agenda: Commission to consider splitting a lot at 44 Watson Drive. This proposed lot split, Case LSP-2026-67100, would divide Parcel 16-78005-010 into multiple parcels. The applicant is Troy Currens.
Arkansas Community Foundation launches $10 million food insecurity fund. The Arkansas Community Foundation, in cooperation with the Walmart Foundation, announced a five-year initiative to address food insecurity, anchored by a $10 million grant from the Walmart Foundation.
McAuley Place development to welcome first residents in October. The McAuley Place development in Bentonville, which aims to offer affordable living options for teachers, will see its first residents move in next month.
Arkansas Department of Transportation to remove political signs from right-of-ways. The Arkansas Department of Transportation reminded candidates and their supporters that placing campaign signs on highway right-of-ways is unlawful and the department will remove them.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Walmart CEO addresses rumors about digital labels and AI pricing. Walmart CEO John Furner is pushing back on rumors regarding the retail giant's new pricing technology and its use of digital labels and AI.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 25, 2026
item.description:
The Benton County Quorum Court approved the creation of a fund for the Sheriff's Office's partnership with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
Benton county Quorum court approves fund for ICE program. The Benton County Quorum Court approved the creation of a fund for the Sheriff's Office's partnership with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement through its 287(g) Program.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider reducing the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would reduce the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from 1% to 0.5%. This is the second reading of the ordinance.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve purchase of a new tractor for the Street Department. The city is asked to approve a contract for $63,860.36 to purchase a new John Deere 5075M utility tractor with a rotary cutter for use by the Street Department.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve appointment to the bella vista library advisory board. The Mayor's appointment of Julie Driver Grau to the Bella Vista Library Advisory Board would be approved, filling a term ending December 31, 2030.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Fayetteville school board renames performing arts facility. The Fayetteville School District's Performing Arts Center has been renamed in honor of longtime educator Warren Rosenaur.
Fayetteville park reopens after $1 million in improvements. Bryce Davis Park in Fayetteville reopened after the completion of approximately $1 million in park improvements.
Bentonville's Arkade adds 14 startup businesses. Bentonville's Arkade added 14 startup businesses in its first year.
Bentonville nonprofit advances in NASA challenge. Bentonville-based nonprofit research organization Autonomic Resilience Collective advanced to the final stage of a NASA challenge to design a food system for Mars.
VIC Tech appoints Sarah Goforth as chief growth officer. VIC Technology Venture Development, a Fayetteville-based company, named Sarah Goforth as chief growth officer and managing director.
Heartland Whole health launches rural health initiative. A Northwest Arkansas-based nonprofit, Heartland Whole Health, is starting an initiative to address the gap in healthcare access for millions of Americans in rural areas.
Crystal bridges to host Indigenous Arts symposium. Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art will host an Indigenous Arts Symposium next month, featuring Indigenous artists and scholars.
Siloam Springs 'Twin Springs' landmark undergoing construction. A downtown Siloam Springs landmark, 'Twin Springs,' which has been closed to the public for over two decades, is undergoing renovation.
Fayetteville school construction projects on schedule. Ongoing Fayetteville School District projects, including Woodland Junior High, are expected to be completed on schedule.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 24, 2026
item.description:
Brandom Gengelbach will step down as president and CEO of the Bentonville Area Chamber of Commerce on October 31.
Brandom Gengelbach to leave Bentonville chamber leadership. Brandom Gengelbach will step down as president and CEO of the Bentonville Area Chamber of Commerce on October 31, three years after being hired to lead the organization.
Bentonville City Council approves grants for road projects. The Bentonville City Council approved grants to partially fund several planned infrastructure projects in the city.
Bentonville City Council approves new artificial intelligence policy. The Bentonville City Council approved new guidelines for the city's use of artificial intelligence to comply with Arkansas state law.
UL Solutions expands testing at Lowell Retail Center of Excellence. UL Solutions expanded its Retail Center of Excellence in Lowell to include apparel and textiles testing, adding to its existing testing of furniture, toys, and electronics.
Updates provided on Bentonville overpass projects. A Bentonville City Council meeting included status updates on projects designed to improve traffic movement across Interstate 49.
Combined sales tax revenue up in four Northwest Arkansas cities. Bentonville, Fayetteville, Rogers, and Springdale reported a combined monthly sales tax revenue of $9.965 million in September, an increase of 2.35%.
Circle of life to acquire Washington Regional Hospice. Circle of Life will acquire Washington Regional Hospice and purchase the Willard Walker Hospice Home in Fayetteville.
Pay-what-you-can bookshop reopens in downtown Springdale. A nonprofit pay-what-you-can bookshop reopened in downtown Springdale, allowing readers to take books for free or pay what they can.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Centerton food pantry to close after 15 years. The Centerton Food Pantry will close its doors after serving the community for 15 years.
Proposed waste management merger faces challenges in Benton County. Merger negotiators were informed that combining Northwest Arkansas' two solid waste districts faces an uphill climb in Benton County.
Lasang Pinoy restaurant in Rogers makes 50-best list. Lasang Pinoy, a Filipino restaurant in Rogers, represents Arkansas on the New York Times' 2026 list of America's Best Restaurants.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 23, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville City Council approved accepting over $5 million in grants for transportation projects.
Bentonville city council approves accepting over $5 million in transportation grants. The Bentonville City Council approved accepting two grants totaling more than $5 million for transportation projects aimed at enhancing the city's transit infrastructure.
Rogers city council approves Mount hebron road rezoning. The Rogers City Council approved a rezoning for Mount Hebron Road, a decision that followed an earlier denial and left some residents disappointed.
Hotel Vin Rogers opens in Pinnacle Hills. A new hotel, Hotel Vin Rogers, has opened in the Pinnacle Hills area, representing an investment of over $72 million and featuring three food and beverage concepts, an outdoor pool, and more than 10,000 square feet of event space.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 11, 2026, as part of the Big Sugar Classic week.
XNA sees narrow dip in August outbound passenger traffic. Northwest Arkansas National Airport (XNA) experienced its second year-over-year decrease in outbound passenger traffic in August, following two consecutive months of record-high enplanements.
Crystal Bridges announces $250,000 Don Tyson Prize recipient. Crystal Bridges has announced the recipient of the 2026 Don Tyson Prize for the Advancement of American Art, which awards $250,000.
Boys and Girls Club of Benton County to offer free dinner for children and teens. The Boys and Girls Club of Benton County will provide free dinner and snacks for children aged 6-18 starting next year.
NWA Food Bank receives donation to kick off Walmart NW Arkansas Championship week. The Northwest Arkansas Food Bank received a joint donation of $20,000 and 40,000 pounds of protein from Walmart and Tyson Foods to mark the start of the 20th Walmart Northwest Arkansas Championship.
Centerton run to support foster children on October 10. Schuber Mitchell Homes is bringing the Love Running Home 5K & 1-Mile Fun Run to Centerton on October 10, an event designed to support children in foster care.
Acres.com releases housing market data product. Fayetteville-based land intelligence platform Acres.com has launched a new product that offers a nationwide view of housing market supply, pricing, and demand.
Springdale city council approves AI policy. The Springdale City Council has approved a policy to establish guidelines for the city's use of artificial intelligence, as mandated by Arkansas state law.
New York Times lists Rogers Filipino restaurant among U.S.' 50 best. Lasang Pinoy, a Filipino restaurant located at 719 W. Walnut St., Suite 104, in Rogers, was included in The New York Times' recently released list of America's Best Restaurants 2026.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 21, 2026
item.description:
The Siloam Springs city board will consider rezoning 13 acres for a 285-unit apartment development along Arkansas 16 during its October meeting.
Siloam Springs city board to consider rezoning for 285-unit apartment development. The Siloam Springs city Board of Directors is set to consider rezoning about 13 acres along Arkansas 16 to make way for an apartment development during its October meeting.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider reducing the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would amend Ordinance No. 2017-15 to reduce the tax residents pay on prepared food and beverages from one percent (1%) to one-half of one percent (0.5%).
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 201 SW E Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development at 201 SW E Street than the current suburban single-family zoning permits, potentially leading to more varied housing options in the neighborhood.
On the Rogers City Council agenda: Council to amend Ordinance No. 24-04 regarding sewer revenue bond terms. This proposed amendment would revise the terms for the outstanding City of Rogers, Arkansas Sewer Revenue Bond, Series 2024, which could affect the city's financial obligations related to its sewer system.
On the Rogers Water Utilities Commission agenda: Commission to consider approving Resolution 26-25 for a 457(b) Deferred Compensation Plan. This proposed resolution would establish or modify a deferred compensation plan for employees, which could impact their retirement savings.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
University of Arkansas Medical Sciences opens new MS clinic in Fayetteville. The University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences opened a new clinic for MS patients on September 18 in Fayetteville.
Bentonville School District receives highest a-ranking in the state. The Bentonville School District is leading the list of the top school districts in Arkansas with its highest A-ranking.
Arkansas Latinas en Bici hosts community bike ride in Bentonville. Arkansas Latinas en Bici, a local cycle group, hosted a community bike ride event throughout Bentonville on Sunday, September 20, encouraging community members to explore Northwest Arkansas.
UAMS hosts Girlology session for puberty education in Fayetteville. The University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences (UAMS) hosted a 'Girlology' informational session for young girls navigating puberty on Sunday in Fayetteville.
Northwest Arkansas cattle ranch expands operations. The 808 Ranch, located 15 minutes from downtown Bentonville, is expanding its operations and adding technology.
Arkansas basketball SEC-ACC challenge game times announced. The Razorbacks men's team will face North Carolina at 6:30 p.m. Central in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, while the women's team will play Wake Forest at 8 p.m. Central in Fayetteville.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 20, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville's City Council and Finance Committee will meet on September 22 to discuss various city matters.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to reduce the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would amend Ordinance No. 2017-15 to decrease the tax on prepared food and beverages from one percent (1%) to one-half of one percent (0.5%). This change would mean residents pay less tax on prepared food and beverage purchases.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 201 SW E Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development at 201 SW E Street than the current suburban single-family zoning permits, potentially leading to more varied housing options in the neighborhood.
On the Bentonville Finance Committee agenda: Committee to accept a $185,605 grant for the John DeShields Trail design and bidding. This would fund the design and bidding documents for trail improvements along the John DeShields Trail corridor between NE J Street and E Central Avenue.
Northwest Arkansas National Airport shelves hotel and convenience store plans. Plans for a hotel and convenience store at Northwest Arkansas National Airport are on hold due to low developer interest and high interest rates.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 11, 2026.
Maple Leaf acquires don's Canopies. Maple Leaf has completed the acquisition of Don's Canopies, as reported in the Northwest Arkansas business briefs.
Springdale's East Emma Avenue streetscape project to begin in October. A $4.8 million project to improve East Emma Avenue in Springdale is expected to commence at the beginning of October.
Harps Food Stores announces director promotions. Harps Food Stores Inc. has promoted William Haulmark to director of insurance and Will McDoniel to director of AI strategy and innovation.
Grandma Moses exhibition opens at Crystal Bridges. The "Grandma Moses: A Good Day's Work" exhibition, featuring nearly 150 works, has opened at Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art in Bentonville.
Bentonville hosts Clean the Streets Day. The City of Bentonville held a city-wide "Clean the Streets Day" on Saturday, participating in Keep America Beautiful's Great Arkansas Cleanup.
LPGA 5K race returns to Bentonville for Mercy Hospital. The LPGA 5K race returned to Bentonville on Saturday, benefiting Mercy Hospital and including community exercise and the Annual Corporate Challenge.
Benton County holds annual Passport Saturday event. The Benton County Circuit Clerk's Office hosted its annual Passport Saturday event, allowing residents to apply for passports.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 19, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville and Bella Vista city councils will consider various proposals this week.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider reducing the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would amend Ordinance No. 2017-15 to reduce the tax on prepared food and beverages from one percent (1%) to one-half of one percent (0.5%). This change would mean residents pay less tax on restaurant meals and other prepared food items.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 201 SW E Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development at 201 SW E Street than the current suburban single-family zoning permits, potentially leading to more varied housing options in the neighborhood.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to accept $4,000,000.00 in grant funds for Greenhouse Road Improvements. Accepting these grant funds would help pay for construction of improvements on Greenhouse Road between Hwy 12 and Hwy 102, with the city contributing 55% of a $1,000,000.00 local match.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 11, 2026.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 18, 2026
item.description:
A $700 million AWSOM Whole Health Campus broke ground in Northwest Arkansas.
AWSOM Whole Health Campus breaks ground for $700 million facility. A groundbreaking ceremony was held for the $700 million AWSOM Whole Health Campus, bringing specialty healthcare to Northwest Arkansas.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider reducing the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would amend Ordinance No. 2017-15 to reduce the tax on prepared food and beverages from one percent (1%) to one-half of one percent (0.5%). If approved, this would mean a lower tax on meals and drinks purchased in the city.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 201 SW E Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development at 201 SW E Street than currently permitted for single-family homes. The Planning Commission recommended approval with a 7-0 vote.
On the Bentonville Construction Board of Appeals agenda: Board to hear appeal from Burckart Construction. Burckart Construction is appealing a decision made by the Building Fire and Safety department. The board will decide whether to uphold or overturn that decision.
Pea Ridge sidewalk project delayed by protected bats. A sidewalk project along McCulloch Street in Pea Ridge has been stalled due to the presence of protected bats.
Walmart pilots health ambassador program in rural stores. Walmart is testing a health ambassador program in rural stores to explore how pharmacists can provide more personalized health guidance to customers.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Best friends pet resource center and centerton animal services offer adventure buddies day. Best Friends Pet Resource Center and Centerton Animal Services will offer adoptable dogs for fun outings as part of Adventure Buddies Day, a nationwide initiative.
Rogers Public Schools Superintendent Jeff Perry to retire. Rogers Public Schools Superintendent Jeff Perry announced his retirement at the end of the current school year.
University of Arkansas, Fayetteville reports record high graduation rates. The University of Arkansas, Fayetteville is reporting record high four-year and six-year graduation rates.
Northwest Technical Institute reports rising enrollment. Northwest Technical Institute has reported increased interest across many of its skilled trades programs for the fall semester.
Retail experts discuss AI and customer needs in Bentonville. Executives from Walmart Inc., Google LLC, and the National Retail Federation, along with consumer experts, discussed the future of retail and the importance of customer trust.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 17, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville closed a downtown parking lot to begin construction on a new parking garage for Dave Peel Park.
Bentonville closes downtown parking lot for Dave Peel Park garage. Bentonville closed its 110-space public parking lot at 300 E. Central Ave. to make way for a new parking garage. The garage is part of the Dave Peel Park expansion and will add 283 public spaces.
Bentonville Health Care Campus hosts groundbreaking ceremony. Leaders from the Alice L. Walton Foundation, Mercy Health, and the community broke ground on the new Bentonville Health Care Campus.
On the Bentonville Public Art Advisory Board agenda: Board to discuss ongoing collaboration with NWACC. This item is a continuation of previous discussions regarding the partnership between the Public Art Advisory Board and Northwest Arkansas Community College.
On the Rogers Water Utilities Commission agenda: Commission to consider a construction Manager/General contractor (CM/GC) contract for RPCF improvements. This contract would establish an agreement for a construction manager and general contractor to oversee and perform improvements at the Rogers Pollution Control Facility.
On the Bentonville Public Art Advisory Board agenda: Board to review updates on the 2027 Project Plan. This item will provide residents with information on the progress of public art projects planned for 2027.
Peel Compton Foundation names new Bentonville property Central House & Gardens. The Peel Compton Foundation officially named its newest property at 606 Central Avenue as the Central House & Gardens.
Bentonville schools reports increased student enrollment for 2026-27. The Bentonville School Board approved the district's 2026-27 fiscal year budget and noted that the district's enrollment is increasing, contrary to statewide trends.
Aerospace and defense summit held at The Ledger. The Arkansas Aerospace and Defense Alliance's Mid-America Aerospace and Defense Summit took place at The Ledger in Bentonville on August 25-26. The event drew over 300 attendees from approximately 100 companies, government agencies, and universities.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. It is part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Cox customers convert to Spectrum brand. Former Cox customers in Arkansas will see new branding on their bills and service interactions as the integration with Spectrum began on September 16.
J.B. Hunt expects higher costs to reduce Q3 earnings. Lowell-based J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc. expects its third-quarter earnings to fall 5% to 10% from the second quarter due to higher costs.
Crafton Tull promotes Daniel Ellis to chief operating officer. Rogers-based engineering and design firm Crafton Tull promoted Daniel Ellis to chief operating officer.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 16, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Planning Commission approved plans to convert the former home of James "Bud" Walton into a botanical garden.
Bentonville Planning Commission approves botanical garden for Bud Walton home. The Bentonville Planning Commission approved plans to transform a home previously owned by James "Bud" Walton into a new public attraction.
On the Bentonville Public Art Advisory Board agenda: Discussing the NWACC Collaboration. The board will continue discussions on the collaboration with Northwest Arkansas Community College.
On the Rogers Water Utilities Commission agenda: Commission to consider a construction Manager/General contractor contract for Rogers Pollution Control Facility improvements. The Commission is asked to approve a contract for a Construction Manager/General Contractor to oversee improvements at the Rogers Pollution Control Facility.
On the Bentonville Public Art Advisory Board agenda: Reviewing the 2027 Project Plan. The board will receive updates on the progress of the 2027 Project Plan.
UAMS opens telehealth booth at Northwest Arkansas National Airport. The University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences Northwest Regional Campus installed a new telehealth booth at Northwest Arkansas National Airport, offering virtual healthcare access to travelers and staff.
Walmart to test health ambassador program in rural stores. Walmart will test a health ambassador role as part of its ongoing efforts to expand its healthcare business, which includes store pharmacists and telehealth options.
Amazeum expansion to open in November. The Amazeum, a children's museum in Northwest Arkansas, is set to open an expansion in November.
Rogers Superintendent Jeff Perry to exit next June. Superintendent Jeff Perry announced his plans to conclude his tenure with Rogers Public Schools in June.
Fayetteville Animal Services advisory board proposes new shelter location. The Fayetteville Animal Services Advisory Board discussed a potential location for a future animal services facility to present to the city council.
Raising cane's considers replacing Fayetteville location. A Fayetteville Raising Cane's restaurant may relocate, though the planning commission recently voted against approving a permit for a potential new site.
Fayetteville parks to host three ribbon-cuttings for new projects. The Fayetteville Parks and Recreation Department has scheduled multiple ribbon-cutting events in the coming months for completed projects, including a new park.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Fayetteville City Council discusses aquatic center site selection. The Fayetteville City Council held a nearly two-hour discussion regarding the next steps in selecting a site for the aquatic center approved in a recent bond election.
Lowell leaders discuss Flock Safety system but delay changes. A proposed resolution to ban the use of Flock Safety systems in Lowell led to a lengthy discussion among City Council members, but no vote was taken.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 15, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville is seeking applicants to fill vacancies on multiple city boards.
Bentonville seeks applicants for city boards. The city of Bentonville is looking for applicants to fill vacancies on three municipal boards.
Bentonville Planning Commission to consider botanical garden site plan. The Bentonville Planning Commission will consider a site plan for a botanical garden on the former property of an original Walmart executive.
Bentonville warns drivers of Southwest Fourth Street closure. The city of Bentonville is advising drivers of a three-day closure of Southwest Fourth Street this month for sewer tap installation.
Northwest Arkansas Community College receives $680,000 for outdoor recreation spaces. Northwest Arkansas Community College plans to use a $680,000 grant to develop new trails and outdoor recreation spaces on campus.
Harps Food announces CEO transition in early 2027. Springdale-based Harps Food Stores has named J. Max Van Hoose to succeed Kim Eskew, who will step down as CEO and chairman in early 2027.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet September 15. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education will hold a meeting on September 15, 2026, at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11 in Bentonville. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to finance a portion of the 48" Supply Water Transmission Project. This resolution would allow the city to finance a portion of the 48" Supply Water Transmission Project with bonds purchased by the Arkansas Development Finance Authority in the amount of $9,621,360.00, with $887,911.00 of that amount being a principal forgiveness bond.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 201 SW E Street from single-family to neighborhood edge. This proposed rezoning would change the property at 201 SW E Street from allowing only suburban single-family homes to a 'Neighborhood Edge' designation, which typically permits a wider variety of housing types and mixed uses.
On the Rogers Water Utilities Commission agenda: Commission to review financial reports. This is a routine update on the financial status of Rogers Water Utilities.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 14, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Schools Board of Education is scheduled to meet on September 15, 2026, to approve its agenda and recognize individuals.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet on September 15. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education is scheduled to hold a meeting on September 15, 2026, at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building. The agenda includes a welcome, call to order, pledge, roll call, and approval or modification of the agenda.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to finance a portion of the 48" Supply Water Transmission Project. This resolution would allow the city to finance a portion of the 48" Supply Water Transmission Project with bonds purchased by the Arkansas Development Finance Authority in the amount of $9,621,360.00, with $887,911.00 of that principal amount in the form of a principal forgiveness bond.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 201 SW E Street from single-family to neighborhood edge. This proposed rezoning would change the property at 201 SW E Street from allowing only suburban single-family homes to a 'Neighborhood Edge' designation, which typically permits a wider variety of housing types and mixed uses.
On the Bella Vista Board of Zoning Adjustment agenda: Board to consider a variance for a non-residential structure at 19 Cheviot Place. This would allow a detached nonresidential structure at 19 Cheviot Place to be placed differently than current rules allow. This could affect the appearance or use of the property.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11 in Bentonville. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled to take place on October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is part of the larger Big Sugar Classic week.
Bat discovery delays Pea Ridge sidewalk construction. Construction of a sidewalk on McCulloch Street in Pea Ridge is facing delays due to the discovery of bats living in nearby trees.
Pea Ridge leaders plan to preserve Rich family homestead. Pea Ridge leaders are developing plans for a natural park on the property of the former Rich family homestead. Mayor Nathan See aims to preserve the natural setting of the historic site.
Fayetteville City Council to consider vendor for Lake Fayetteville marina shop. The Fayetteville City Council is scheduled to vote on the approval of a new vendor for the Lake Fayetteville marina rental and concession shop. The space has been vacant for approximately nine months.
Fayetteville City Council to consider aquatic center site study funding. The Fayetteville City Council is expected to consider allocating up to $75,000 for an additional assessment of potential site locations for the aquatic center. The aquatic center was approved as part of this year's bond package.
Springdale Fire chief discusses new station for city growth. The Springdale Fire Chief stated that a new fire station is intended to help the department keep pace with the city's growth in residents and expanding city limits.
Simmons Foods CEO discusses generational perspective. Todd Simmons, CEO of Simmons Foods, expressed his focus on a 'generational perspective' in his role. He has been CEO for over a decade.
Washington Regional hires new physicians. Fayetteville-based Washington Regional has announced new physician hires. Rogers-based Generations Bank also announced new hires and promotions.
Springdale hosts annual Squirrel Cook-off. The annual World Champion Squirrel Cook-off returned to Springdale on Saturday. The event featured various squirrel-based dishes.
Nonprofit builds beds for Northwest Arkansas children. A local nonprofit chapter constructed 250 beds for children in Northwest Arkansas. The organization aims to ensure that no children in the area sleep on the floor.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 13, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Schools Board of Education will meet on September 15, 2026, to approve its agenda and recognize individuals.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet September 15. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education will hold a meeting on September 15, 2026, at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building. The agenda includes a welcome, roll call, approval of the agenda, and recognitions.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11 in Bentonville. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is part of the larger Big Sugar Classic week.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to finance a portion of the 48" Supply Water Transmission Project. This resolution would allow the city to finance a portion of a large water transmission project with bonds purchased by the Arkansas Development Finance Authority, including a principal forgiveness bond of $887,911.00.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 201 SW E Street from suburban single-family to neighborhood edge.. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development at 201 SW E Street, moving from single-family homes to a neighborhood edge style within a walkable neighborhood.
On the Bella Vista Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider requiring 200-foot distance between short-term rentals in residential zones. This proposal would mean that new short-term rentals in residential areas would need to be at least 200 feet away from any existing short-term rental. This could affect where new short-term rental properties can be established in the city.
Centerton's downtown master plan requires public-private partnerships. Centerton officials state that the city's Downtown Master Plan will necessitate public-private partnerships for its revitalization and expansion. The city is currently determining the next steps after about a year of planning.
Colliers Arkansas announces additions and promotion to Northwest Arkansas team. Colliers Arkansas has announced four new additions and one promotion to its Northwest Arkansas team. The team is based in Rogers at 3503 S. 55th St., Suite 200.
GoodWorks hosts inaugural Day of service with 14 nonprofits. GoodWorks, a volunteer center of the Jones Center, hosted its first Day of Service on Saturday. The event connected residents with 14 local nonprofits to support volunteerism across Northwest Arkansas.
Volunteers build 250 beds for Northwest Arkansas children. Volunteers in Bentonville built 250 beds for children in Northwest Arkansas as part of the annual Bunks Across America event by Sleep in Heavenly Peace. This initiative aims to provide beds for children who need them.
XNA transitions from zero security to modern TSA standards. Northwest Arkansas National Airport (XNA) has evolved from having no security to implementing modern Transportation Security Administration (TSA) standards. This change reflects the normalization of security procedures for travelers.
Concerns raised about ICE operations' impact on Northwest Arkansas businesses. Irma Chavez, founder of the Arkansas Hispanic Chamber of Commerce, has expressed concerns about the impact of nationwide enhanced immigration enforcement on Northwest Arkansas businesses. She noted that small and family-owned businesses are particularly vulnerable.
Northwest Arkansas Food Bank and cystic fibrosis foundation hold fundraising events. The Northwest Arkansas Food Bank held its second annual Flavor of Giving fundraiser on August 27 at Osage House in Cave Springs. The Cystic Fibrosis Foundation also hosted an event to raise funds for local causes.
Erik Dees releases new book on values-driven leadership. Erik Dees, a partner at Fayetteville-based Milestone Leadership, has released a new book titled "Keeper of the Culture." The book challenges leaders to redefine success and what constitutes strong leadership.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 12, 2026
item.description:
Benton County has reached exceptional drought status for the first time since 2012.
Benton County reaches exceptional drought status. Parts of Benton County have been upgraded to exceptional drought status, marking the third time the area has experienced such severe dryness since 2012.
Benton washington regional public water authority lifts irrigation moratorium. The Benton Washington Regional Public Water Authority has lifted a weeks-long moratorium on lawn watering for its customers.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet on September 15. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education will hold a meeting on September 15, 2026, at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building, 500 Tiger Blvd.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 201 SW E Street from single-family to neighborhood edge. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development than suburban single-family homes at 201 SW E Street, potentially increasing housing density in the area.
On the Bella Vista Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider new distance requirements for short-term rentals. American Airlines adds new one-stop flights from XNA to europe in 2027. American Airlines announced it will add new one-stop flights from Northwest Arkansas National Airport (XNA) to several European destinations in 2027.
Work continues on Fayetteville competition stadium remodel. Work is continuing on the remodel of the competition stadium in Fayetteville, which will be the future home turf for the Fayetteville School District's junior high teams.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville, as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Former Tyson Foods executive named CFO at Hormel Foods. A former Tyson Foods executive has been named the chief financial officer at Hormel Foods.
Bentonville girls golf team wins fort smith tournament. The Bentonville girls golf team won the Fort Smith tournament.
Bentonville tennis prevails over Rogers squad. The Bentonville tennis team prevailed over Rogers in a match between two top teams in the 6A-West Conference at Memorial Park.
Japanese artist behind Crystal Bridges 'Infinity mirrored Room' dies at 97. Yayoi Kusama, the artist behind the Infinity Room at the Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art, has died at 97.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 27, 2026
item.description:
Southwest D Street in Bentonville will close until October 2 for infrastructure work.
Southwest D Street in Bentonville to close through October 2. Southwest D Street between Southwest 20th Street and Southwest 24th Street will be closed for infrastructure work until October 2.
Bentonville City Council approves morning star schoolhouse property donation. The Bentonville City Council approved the donation of the Morning Star Schoolhouse property, which the Parks and Recreation Department plans to revitalize.
Bentonville City Council amends noise regulations. The Bentonville City Council approved amendments to a city ordinance concerning noise regulations following complaints from businesses and residents.
Triton Ventures opens headquarters in Bentonville. Bentonville AI startup Triton Ventures opened its new headquarters at North ROC, an office and coworking campus.
Scott Family Amazeum to open expansion this fall. The Scott Family Amazeum in Bentonville will open approximately 34,740 square feet of new indoor and outdoor space this fall, adjacent to its existing 50,000-square-foot museum.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Pasture in Lowell sells for $4.3 million. More than 12 acres of pasture along Interstate 49 in Lowell recently sold for $4.33 million, equating to $348,479 per acre.
August sales tax revenue falls in Bentonville, Fayetteville, Rogers, and Springdale. Sales tax revenue reported in August for Bentonville, Fayetteville, Rogers, and Springdale totaled $10.001 million, a 0.12% decrease from the same month last year.
Walton children to be inducted into business hall of fame. Rob Walton, Alice Walton, Jim Walton, and the late John Walton, children of Walmart founders Sam and Helen Walton, will be inducted into the Arkansas Business Hall of Fame.
Rogers City Council meeting cancelled. The Rogers City Council meeting scheduled for September 8, 2026, has been cancelled.
Rogers fire Pension and Relief Board to meet. The Fire Pension and Relief Board will hold a meeting from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM at 301 W. Chestnut Street in Rogers.
